evidence: North ridge described as third class; trip report scrambled class 2/3 to the summit; a winter party met some 4th-class steps.
Scatter Lake route called a Class 2 scramble (scree/talus then short ridge walk); one summary of the SummitPost page mentions Class 3 along the ridge from the saddle.
Mountain Project lists East Gully at Agathla Tower (Frenchman Coulee, Vantage) as 3rd class.
Mountain Project and SummitPost both grade the North Ridge 5.3; MP calls a 50-60 ft 4th-class pitch the crux.
FKT route page: 'mixed 3rd and 4th class climbing to gain summits' and 4th-class downclimbs; trip reports put Kimtah Class 2+, Katsuk and Cosho Class 3, with class 4 sections on the traverse.
Maintained trail (Round Mountain #1529 to Nason Ridge) to a staffed lookout; 10 mi RT, 2,600 ft gain.
Northeast face via a ~45-degree snow gully then rock of 'only moderate difficulty (class 4 but mostly class 3)'.
Trip report titles the West Ridge '3rd'; other sources call it a hike with easy scrambling (class 2 from the south peak).
Mountain Project: 5.6 WI2 Steep Snow, Grade III, 1,200 ft, 40-50 degree couloir.
Mountaineers rate it a Technical 3 scramble: up south slopes to the ridge east of the summit, then along the ridge.

Mountain Project: Easy 5th, Grade III, about 150 ft of 4th and easy 5th to the summit; the summit tower's chockstone line is cited as 5.2; one party felt the first moves out of the notch might be 5.7.
Standard route rated Class 3/4: sustained class 3+ near the top with short class 4 sections.
Easiest route is the North Ridge, class 3 scrambling (first ascent 1933, Ulrichs and Falkenburg).
Easy ridge climbing to a false summit and on to the top; Mountaineers schedule it as a scramble (Technical 3 in their system).
Beckey-Fielding 1967 North Face Buttress (originally NCCS V, F8, A4) now climbed free at IV, 5.10, 7 pitches of class 5; no source found giving a letter grade.
Easiest route is a class 3 scramble from the southwest; the final ~100 m from Church Lake requires scrambling.

The slab itself is unrated easy friction ('only using our hands in a few spots'); the finish is via the summit block, which the two Mega Slab routes on Mountain Project and the SW Face reports grade 5.6. One party called its summit chimney 'pretty easy but exposed'.
East ridge is an easy Class 2-3 scramble; the crux is ~30 ft of exposed Class 2-3 slab; Mountaineers rate it Technical 4.
East side steep and mossy, mostly Class 3 with one or two Class 4 moves.
Wildhorse Creek / west ridge route: Class 2-3 to Class 3, exposed scramble up blocky ledges to the summit pinnacle.
First ascent route (Farr and Winder, July 1931); no online source gives a class for the northwest ridge. The easiest route on the peak is class 3-4, so this ridge is at least that.
Summit block starts with an unprotectable 5.7-5.8 boulder move (often done with a shoulder stand)
Myrtle Lake route given as class 2-3 with route finding (another description: all class 2)
East Buttress from Wing Lake: gully system with a series of Class 3 and 4 steps on fairly solid rock
MP: Easy 5th, Grade II; guides and TRs: II 5.3; one page 'Class 4 - 5.4'; consensus around 5.2-5.3
Mostly class 3 with exposed class 4 moves to reach the summit
East/NE ridge scramble mostly class 3 with exposure on loose rock near the top; summit also described as class 2/3
Route rated Class 3 and 4: Class 3-4 rock right of the gully, Class 4 to the notch and along the loose crest
Overview describes the Mary Green Glacier standard route, rated Class 3-4
Climbed as part of the V 5.7/5.8 three-summit traverse; the NE Buttress itself 'in the 5.7 range' on or around the crest
FA report: Northwest Ridge V 5.8, solid 5.8 on the last two pitches
Route on Booker from the Booker-Buckner col described as class 3 with tricky route finding; the col itself is steep hard snow
Standard route: mostly exposed class 3 with class 4 crux moves ~50 ft below the summit; 'steep, loose, exposed 4th class'
Scramble from Hemlock Pass up the SW side: exposed rock with good holds; summit block mostly class 2/3 on the path of least resistance
Mostly class 2 with a bit of class 3; difficulty should never exceed Class 3
40-50 deg snow and ice, Grade II (some say III); neighbouring NE Face listed III AI2
Scree/talus chute on the SW face to the south ridge, then a short 3rd-class scramble to the summit; one guide service lists 'Class 4 rock' and steep snow
No online source found; record describes three leads of low-to-mid class 5 granite then Class 3-4
Sloan-Cadet ridge traverse rated Class 3
NE ridge described as class 3, but a 2024 TR reports exposed class 3-4 with a class 4 crux around 5,200 ft
Class 2 overall; summit is a ~15-ft steep exposed slab boulder needing an exposed class 3 move
Broad scree/talus NW couloir gains the north ridge; the true (south) summit block needs ~20 ft of 4th class/low 5th
Middle summit is class 3; the higher south summit is a spire needing a short 4th class/low 5th pitch (~20 ft)
Carne Mountain Trail is YDS Class 1 to the broad summit
Northeast Ridge listed as 3rd class alpine
SE route offered as a shorter standard-route alternative finishing up a gully; class 3 with harder 3-4 options on climber's left
Standard route: upper west ridge 'pretty much 3rd class to the summit'; some descriptions say class 3 and 4
FA news: Fight or Flight, IV 5.10+, ~1,400 ft on the north face
MP: Southeast Face, Easy 5th; elsewhere a single low-fifth-class pitch, or listed Class 4
Scramble with two minor Class 3+ bits and one Class 4 step-across over the summit chasm
Mountaineers: 2-3 pitch Class 4; guidebook class 4, one write-up says it feels like low 5th and most parties rope one pitch.
MP: AI2 Steep Snow, 4 pitches; Alpine Institute: Grade II, mostly 50-65 degrees with one short ~80 degree step.
From the 5500 ft cirque the rock face needs one or two 4th class moves; ridge to summit called 4th class.
A dirt road and trail lead to the tower-topped summit; a walk-up.
MP: East Face / Rebel Yell 5.10, 6 pitches, Grade III; trip report also gives 5.10.
Glacier Lake route: mostly class 2 with a class 3 chimney to the summit.
SW/south side reports: class 2 up to mediocre class 3 rock on the south ridge; one moderately exposed class 3 step; none report 5th class.
Easy to the summit block; a couple of class 4 moves needed to top it (class 3-4 pitches some parties rope).
MP lists it as 3rd class.
MP: 5.10a/b, 5 pitches; top of range is 5.10b.
Easiest route on Colchuck is class 3 from the Colchuck col; no source documents a separate 'East Ridge'.
MP: Steep Snow, 'a couple low class 5 moves to the top'; Mountaineers: Grade II, snow to 45 degrees, Class 3-4 or easy Class 5 where it joins the North Buttress.
MP: Snow, Grade II, steep snow to 60+ degrees; SummitPost rates it AI2-3; conditions range from a snow climb to thin ice and mixed.
FA: M5 R AI4+, about 1000 ft (Haley-Hart 2015).
Easiest route is the West Ridge: glacier/snow climb and a class 3 scramble; a report found no class 4 moves.
Steep class 3 with a couple of short (10-15 ft) class 4 ledges; one ledge can be bypassed on steep snow.
SE Glacier route: a class 3-4 gully to a notch on the NE ridge, then mostly class 3 to the summit.
Exposed class 3 with a few class 4 moves.
Easiest route is the Southeast Ridge, class 2 (narrow but only class 2).
AAC: one new east-face route goes straight up from the glacier at class 3-4.
MP: 5.11a/b PG13; top of range is 5.11b.
MP: III WI4, 7 pitches; WI3-3+ then sustained WI4 crux; upper mixed pitches 'go at 5.4 in the summer'.
Mountaineers route page (via search): Cutthroat Peak/Southeast Buttress, Grade III 5.8; twin gullies to notch, 'Tarzan Jump', mixed 3rd-5th class to summit.
Basic glacier climb on crevassed Dark Glacier, then exposed loose Class 2-3 scramble to summit; Class 2-3 forested slopes below.

Gorge Creek south buttress/ridge reports: 'reasonable Class 2-3 scrambling, except for some slime-coated rock slabs near the top'; rope carried but not used; run by Mountaineers as an alpine scramble.
Wikipedia: easiest route class 3; SummitPost log entries: nothing beyond class 3 on the right line, class 4 if off-route; WTA 'Class 3 or 4'.
SummitPost: from the ~7,500 ft col on the SE ridge scramble to summit (Class 3-4); both main routes are Class 4. One trip report belayed a short 'Class 5.0' first pitch of the summit block.
Abegg: Dome Glacier route '3rd Class'; SummitPost: 35-degree glacier and a few third class moves; Mountaineers: Basic Glacier Climb, Technical 2, exposed summit rock arete some parties belay.
FA trip report title: Dome Peak S. Face - Indian Summer (III 5.10), FA 9/2/2011; 8 pitches, ~1000 ft.
Climber Kyle: 'Dot Mountain was an easy walkup'; the Class 3 (and bypassable Class 4) scrambling reported is on the Dot-Lago ridge traverse, not Dot's own summit.
MP: East ridge 3rd; SummitPost: Aasgard Pass, Snow Creek Glacier (~30 deg), then easy class 3 scramble to summit.
Hidden Couloir is the first couloir of Triple Couloirs: ~800 ft of 40-50 degree snow and ice; no separate ice grade found (Triple Couloirs overall WI3 M3, its crux is above this couloir).
MP: Gerber-Sink 5.7 WI3+ M4 Steep Snow; summer mostly 4th/low 5th with a couple of 5.7 cruxes, winter WI3-4 ~M4.
Pandora's Box: short steep snow couloir to ~45 degrees from Colchuck Col, crampons needed, no fall zone; then scramble.
MP: Triple Couloirs WI3 M3 Steep Snow R, Grade IV, ~2,500 ft.
SummitPost: easiest route Southwest Face Class 3; West Route exposed Class 3 scrambling with Class 3 all-hands moves near the summit.
Standup Creek joins the same upper ridge; summit described as a moderate class 2 scramble.
FA (Abegg/Wallace 2009): III AI3, 1200 ft couloir, 40 degrees steepening to ~60 at the top, ending with a bit of 5.7 rock.
Trip report: final cliff band 'described as class 4' (easy chimney moves), and one party used a short low-5th (5.3) step on the headwall; SummitPost mentions short class 3 rock steps.
Standard route east ridge from Prusik Pass: walk-up with ~15 ft of 3rd class to the NE summit; one report calls the block Class 4.
Wikipedia: easiest route class 2 scrambling; record and trip reports describe a short loose 3rd-class gully below the summit; top of Class 2-3.

South Peak standard ('least committing', per the Cascade Alpine Guide) route from Hozomeen Lake: Class 3-4 scrambling and a chimney, with a short 5.6 wall below the summit as the crux.
Southwest Buttress (Culbert/Purdey 1968): Grade IV, class 5.7-5.10a, hard to protect, very few ascents.
MP: East Ridge 'Easy 5th'; trip report: Class 3-4 ridge then about 10 ft of 'probably Class 5.3' dihedral on the upper east face.
Mountain Project: West Face 5.6 (2001), technically harder than the East Ridge; the record's own rock_grade and breakdown also say 5.6.
Easiest route on Hurry-up Peak is class 3 scrambling.
Ruth-Icy via the Icy Glacier and the SE peak's NW ridge: steep, loose, exposed, with a Class 4 knife-edge summit ridge; SummitPost rates the route Class 4.
Easiest route class 2, with a few short Class 3 sections near the summit.
No published grade for the 1983 original line was found; MP describes the shared upper buttress as class 4-low fifth, and the record's breakdown says 'Low 5th'.
The traverse from the Old Snowy col is mostly class 2, with a few class 3 sections depending on conditions.
A crevassed glacier, then about 700 ft of headwall snow up to 60°; no ice grade is published.
Northeast Glacier (Beckey party, 1978) is listed without a grade; the AAJ describes a badly broken north-side glacier where objective danger forced the party onto a ridge to the right.
CJ Couloir (a long snow couloir, icy late season) to the East Ridge, then up to about 1,000 ft of 3rd-4th class rock and heather to the summit.
The NE Rib is usually done via the 1957 start at V 5.6; the 1951 start is less direct and 'has a scary 5.7 pitch'.
Clean Break IV 5.10b/c, 15 pitches; the pitch-1 splitter is the 5.10c crux.
South-face route is Class 2+ overall, but the final 250 ft 'will certainly involve some class 4' up one of the ribs or gullies.
From the Klawatti-Austera col, Class 3 scrambling leads to The Smokestack, which is bypassed; the record says Class 4 in spots.
Kololo Peaks are Class 2 climbs; the White Chuck Glacier route passes a couple of minor Class 2+ cliff bands; the difficulty is glacier travel and approach.
Columbia Glacier route: about 50 ft of loose class 3+ exiting the glacier, a summit block with moat-stemming and some exposed 4th class; other accounts call the final section exposed class 3.
East Ridge from La Bohn Gap is a Class 2 route, listed as the easiest on the peak.
Lake Mountain is a class 2 scramble with route finding (no single move needs hands); several gullies of similar difficulty.
Mountain Project: Classic Route 4th class; the easiest route on Lane is class 4 scrambling (steep upper class 3 with a 4th-class finish).
Mountain Project lists The Fly as 'Mod. Snow', the easiest of the three couloirs; the record's breakdown has AI1 with one WI2-/AI1+ step.
Mountain Project: Spontaneous Distraction 5.10a/b, 4 pitches.
Goatshead Spire (Goodman/Mason, 1982) is listed with no grade; MP notes that Lemah's summits all have class 4-low 5th routes.
MP: Sidewinder (Southwest Corner) 5.9+, Grade II, 5 pitches; P3a wide flaring crack is the crux.
MP: Liberty Ridge Grade IV, AI2-3 steep snow; crux is the steep ice above Thumb Rock / Black Pyramid.
Described as a rock scramble via the Southeast Ridge to the Lichtenhorn; the craggy west summit is reported as Class 3.
Only a trip-report entry (rock climb via West Face-West Rib) found, with no rating; the spire's wrap-around is reported elsewhere as loose Class 3.
SummitPost route page and Lemke both title it 'South Face 5.5', 3 pitches (5.4, 5.5, Class 3); one TR mentions 5.6.
Easiest route is the Northeast Face, Class 3-4 scrambling; record notes short belayed 3rd-4th class pitches.
MP: 3rd, Mod. Snow; TRs give 400-800 ft of Class 2-3 rock and a short exposed Class 3 summit block. One TR calls the ramp Class 3-4.
MP: Cowlitz/Ingraham Glaciers 3rd, Steep Snow. The Mountaineers' South Face variant instead climbs several pitches of Class 4-low 5th rock.
Standard Fryingpan/Whitman (East Shoulder) route: MP 3rd, Mod. Snow; short exposed Class 3 summit block.
TR: easy Class 2 ledges to the ridge, an exposed Class 3+ traverse beneath the summit, and a final Class 3 scramble.
From Luna Col the broad south ridge is Class 2 talus to the false summit; the traverse to the true summit is Class 3 and the crux.
MP: 5.12 Grade IV, 11 pitches, crux P7 roof 5.12-; the FA's blog titles it 5.12b.
Banana (NE) Couloir: 2,000 ft of 40-45 degree snow below, 45-50 above, 50 degrees at the very top; booted, with no ice grade.
South Ridge rated Class 3-4: an easy heather ridge to the false summit, then Class 3-4 broken ledges that corkscrew the summit's east side.
No route-specific rating found beyond the record's Class 3-4 heather gullies; the neighbouring routes to the same summit are Class 3-4 and Class 4.
MP: East Ridge 'Easy Snow'; easiest route Class 2; Mountaineers rate it a Basic Glacier Climb. The crux is the exposed snow knife-edge.
MP: Northwest Ice Couloir AI2-3 Steep Snow; a fall TR calls it WI3 in lean conditions.
SummitPost: the standard (only non-technical) route to the main summit is easy class 3; a trip report calls the crux class 2/3; no source gives class 4.
SummitPost: West Ridge is the standard Class 4 route; trip report: exposed Class 4 gully ~100 ft below the summit.
West side of the summit block: a couple of class 3 slab moves and one steep move; an easier class 3 gully on the SE side; harder 4th/5th lines are optional.
Mountain Project: 4th class, Grade II, Easy Snow; a mellow 3rd-4th class scramble to the exposed summit block after the Terror Glacier snow gully.
The gully to the west ridge starts with steep class 3/4 climbing; reports say the upper 250 ft will 'certainly involve some class 4'; then an exposed ridge crest.
Only description found: ~5 short pitches of loose blocky climbing, finishing with 'wonderful easy climbing up cracks and knobs'; no number given anywhere.
SummitPost gives 5.3; Mountaineers: 3rd/4th class with a short mid-5th pitch to the summit-ridge notch; Mountain Project: Easy 5th, 2 pitches.
Easiest (North Col) route: steep snow and a 5.6 chimney (now bolted) to the summit, then a ramp and Class 3 (some avoidable Class 4).
The easiest route is class 3 scrambling; none of its routes are technical, plus ~45 degree snow in season.
Mountain Project: AI2-3 Steep Snow, Grade III, 4,700 ft; moderate snow/ice with short, steeper icefall sections that may need a belay.
The Lava Glacier route reaches ~45 degrees on the upper headwall, Grade III; Mountain Project grades the Lava Glacier 'Mod. Snow'. No ice grade given.

Mountain Project: 'Steep Snow'; a 40 degree glacier, then a 45 degree headwall; an optional 40-ft 60-70 degree snow/ice step below Piker's Peak.

Mountain Project: North Ridge (West Face) AI1-2 Steep Snow.
Mountain Project: South Spur 'Easy Snow'; the relatively easy, non-technical standard route.

Mountaineers alpine scramble: technical difficulty 3; scramble the ridge west from Mount Annette's south ridge to the summit.
SummitPost: a moderate 5,200 ft crevassed glacier climb with a bergschrund to cross, Grade III; no rock or ice grade.
Mountain Project: 'Mod. Snow', not technically difficult; the solid, well-featured rock section is 3rd class with a fixed hand line.
Mountain Project: Cockscomb Ridge T 4th, AI2-3 PG13. No 5th-class rock; the graded crux is AI2-3 ice.
Mountain Project: Coleman/Deming Glacier 'Mod. Snow'; a non-technical glacier route finishing on the Roman Wall (~35-40 degrees).

Mountain Project: Squak Glacier 'Easy Snow'; steady snow slopes on the south side up to ~35-40 degrees.
Wikipedia: the easiest route is class 2 scrambling; the record's own breakdown is Class 2 throughout.
SummitPost: North Ridge 5.9, Grade III; ~150 m of 5.8-5.9 R climbing on compact granite to gain the crest.

West Route: a large ramp up the face to the summit ridge, Class 2-3; a west-ridge rock band variant needs a few Class 3-4 moves, plus a steep exposed snowfield near the top.
Corkscrew route from the Clark-Johnson col on ledges around the S and E sides, finishing with an exposed class 3/4 slot up the north side of the summit block; usually a 60-ft rappel to descend.
The easiest route is class 2 via the Hayden Pass trail, with a brief stretch of Class 3 scrambling on the west side of the summit.

The Olympic Mountains climbing guide rates the Finger Traverse 3rd class (a finger crack along a downsloping ledge, often roped); the route to the summit then needs a couple of 4th class moves on the summit block.
The South Chute standard route is rated Class 3, Grade II, but sources note a couple of required 4th class moves on the summit block after exposed 3rd class scrambling.

SummitPost and an NWHikers trip report: West Arete YDS 5.5, Grade III; Mountaineers lists it as Grade III 5.4. Mostly 4th and low 5th, ~1,100 ft.
Abegg (descent): grassy 3rd class ledges with occasional 4th class moves and one or two short 5th class downclimbing moves; no number given.
SW side described as a talus boulder hop; easiest of Tupshin/Devore/Flora, no climbing gear.

4th-class route down the east side toward Chiwawa; the ridge has a 4th-class chimney.

Common route: Lake Ann trail to the ridge, then class 2 scramble; one trip report found a class 3/4 approach to the saddle off the usual line.
Easiest route: class 2 southwest slope.

Conrad route joins the Meade Glacier finish, which MP grades 3rd class with Easy Snow.

MP: West Route, 4th class, R, lots of loose rock.
MP: 4th, AI1-2, Grade II; final ~200 ft of AI2 ice is the crux.

MP: Easy Snow, axe and crampons; summit reached by a snow chute; no technical crux.

East Peak reached by an easy Class 2 gully; not technically difficult, but steep slippery heather.

MP: Easy 5th; trip reports describe ~15 ft of 5.0 on the summit block.

Final approach is a class 4 scramble up a knife-edge ridge with a couple of class 4 moves.
Short class-4-ish section at the Hidden Ramp; otherwise class 2-3.

Ridge walk with class 2 sections; hard class 3 to the summit.

Principally Class 2 from the south with a short, low-exposure class 3 summit block.
Class 2 boulder scramble along the summit ridge; listed class 2/3.
North Ridge-North Cirque-NE Ridge: mostly class 2-3 with a short, very exposed class 4 segment; easiest route on the peak class 4.

Easiest route listed as class 2; trip reports note a loose, sharp rocky summit but no ropes needed.
Rated Class 3 to 3+ (Wikipedia/trip report) and Class 4 (WTA); the 'hidden gully' option has some 5th-class moves at the top, the ledge option is 3+.

MP: Tower Arete 4th class; follows the North Tower ridge avoiding its 5.8 pitches
MP: North Face 5.7 (winter WI3- M4-5); SummitPost describes 5.4 gully pitches then 5.5 crest pitches; commonly cited as III 5.7
Traverse involves Class 3 or 4 on Cloudy Peak's east ridge (Class 3 bypass to the south); Cloudy's summit block needs a couple of Class 4 moves
Class 3-4 on the trail line beside the crest, Class 4-5 if staying on the crest
MP: West Ridge 4th, Grade II; 5th-class options abound but are optional
East side: 2-3 pitches of easy/moderate class 5, also described as mid-fifth; no number found
Mostly Class 2 boot path, then a Class 2-3 ledge system/easy 3rd class to the summit

SummitPost East Face (Right Side): ~5 pitches Class 3 to 5.4; peak page says the summit block needs Class 4 if not low 5th; Mountaineers calls the snow-finger finish Class 3 ledges with rope/pro advisable.
Easiest route is a scramble via the SW shoulder; trip reports describe a short roughly Class 3 band of mossy dirt-covered ledges low on the route, the rest Class 2.

Easiest route listed as Southwest Route Class 4; a recent trip report found Class 2-3 to the ridge with an exposed crest needing a hand line to the true summit, plus moderately steep snow on the pocket glacier.
Mountain Project: Southwest Scramble 4th class from the Pinnacle Saddle trail; other reports call it Class 3 or Class 3/4.
Mountain Project: Southwest Scramble 4th class, loose rock and scree above the Pinnacle Saddle trail.
SummitPost lists rock difficulty 5.4; Mountaineers: Class 3 rock and steep snow early season, final rock band to the summit low Class 5.
Rainy Lake route: brush, mossy slabs, then Class 3 (one report says 3/4) scrambling once on the ridge; Mountaineers list it as a scramble.
Primus from the south and west is a Class 2 walk-up; parties from the Eldorado/McAllister side unrope and scramble snow-covered talus to the summit.
FA party's report: 5.10+ C1 overall, but pitch 5 is the 5.11a final pitch shared with Solid Gold; P3 has a 15 ft aid section (C1, maybe 5.12- free).
Mountain Project lists Stanley-Burgner 5.10a and a 2021 report calls it 5.10-; older sources and one trip report give 5.9+.
Rated YDS Class 2 ('this one's a walk'); Class 3 (avoidable Class 4) only on the ridge traverse toward Dot Mountain.
Crater Lake side reaches the same summit block, which goes at Class 3 via a short passage under the boulders; the ridge itself is Class 2-3.
Very loose gully to the crest (Class 2+), easy ridge scramble; summit block looks 4th/5th but a tunnel on the SW side leads to a Class 3 scramble to the top.
West slope scramble alternates Class 2 and Class 3 at 30-40 degrees with little exposure.
Mountain Project: 4th class; several Class 3 pitches, optional Class 4/low-5th direct summit finish.
Former lookout reached by an old trail switchbacking up the SE talus slope from Four Point Lake; described as a Class 1 walk-up with trail to the summit.
South (true) summit reputed Class 3 or 4 from the col between the summits; another report calls it Class 2/3 with a very exposed step-across move.
Standard SE ridge via Beauty Creek: mile-long loose ridge scramble that does not exceed Class 3 (Class 2-3).
Only trip report describes the NE ridge from the Howard-Rock col as a snow climb and rock scramble, with no class given.
Summer: steep trail to the summit, non-technical with no scrambling or exposure; in winter it becomes a winter scramble with a narrow, sometimes corniced ridge to the true summit.
Winter route: short trail, then 5,000 ft of steep untracked forest and snow; finishes on the same summit ridge as the NW ridge (exposed rock and snow). No class given beyond 'winter scramble'.
Fourth of July Pass then bootpath; the final 6,600-7,200 ft is a Class 2-3 scramble on a steep, somewhat exposed rock and grass slope.
Mountain Project: 4th class, Grade II, Easy Snow; crux is a 100 ft low-4th-class summit gully on Icy Peak after Class 2-3 terrain.
Mostly a walk-up with easy, minimally crevassed glacier travel; Mountain Project rates the North Face 'Easy Snow'.
Easiest route on Ruth Peak is a Class 3 scramble, usually climbed from the Bailey Range Traverse.
Mountain Project: Quien Sabe Glacier 4th class, Easy Snow; the Mountaineers describe a loose-rock summit scramble after an exposed snow traverse.
West face from the South Cascade Glacier side: snow, a bergschrund crossing with some 4th-class rock, then Class 2/3 ledge and face to the summit. No 5th class reported.
Standard SW slopes/ridge rated Class 2 by one source and Class 3 by another; loose gully, optional snow couloir.
Main summit is mostly steep Class 3/4 rock and brush, with one short pitch that should be belayed; north summit is Class 2/3 from Weden Pass.

From the Roman Wall saddle, parties traverse to the south and front-point steep icy slopes to an exposed summit ridge with rime-ice knobs; in good snow the west ridge is described as a friendly ridge walk.

Mountain Project rates the Squak Glacier 'Easy Snow', Grade III; it joins the Easton route at the Sherman Crater rim, and the final climb to Sherman's summit is steep, icy front-pointing to an exposed rime-ice ridge.
East Ridge: broad NNE gully to the crest east of the Balanced Rock, then blocks and sandy benches westward to the summit, Class 3-4.
Mountain Project: West Ridge 5.5, 3 pitches; one report calls the final 5.4 crack 'comically sandbagged'.
Mountain Project: 4th class, Steep Snow; summit rocks variously Class 3 or 4, with a Class 4 chimney and mantle to the true summit.
45-50 degree neve and ice face, ice screws and pickets required (Mountaineers: intermediate ice climb), then a short rock scramble to the summit. No ice grade given.
Climbers Guide to the Olympic Mountains (as quoted online): the Incisor's only route is 5.4 along the knife-edge ridge; no scramble line. Royal Basin routes range Class 3 to 5.8.
SummitPost: all four Pleiades are reportedly 3rd class scrambles, on loose rock.
The Mountaineers: Temple West Side, two-pitch basic rock climb, Grade II+, 5.6.
MP 5.10a/b; pitch 4 v-slot is 5.10b - top of range.
MP: original grading 'WI3 low 5th, 50-70 degree ice (1st pitch variation)', Grade II, 5 pitches.
Wikipedia: easiest route class 4; one report calls the east-ridge crux 'stiff 4th class'; one party roped a 'low-5th class pinnacle'.
AAJ: west face of Middle Triad is the crux of the Triad Traverse, 5.6 R.
Class 2-3 scrambling above the snowfield; ladders give access to the otherwise 5th-class summit block.
Trip report: 'The final obstacle was a Class 4 chimney straight up the face'.
East Peak via NE ridge is class 3 (Wikipedia: 3+), with reports of a loose Class 4 section to gain the ridge; top of range Class 4.
SummitPost: West Tower is the hardest summit (class 5); trip report: easiest routes on Main/Middle/West are Class 3/4/5, West Queen's final pitch 'Class 5.7ish' on questionable rock with sketchy pro.
SummitPost: north face is granite with 600 ft of class 5, first climbed 1972; no YDS number published.
Southeast route rated 3rd; reports say the summit block goes at Class 3 on the right line (Class 4 only off-route).
Couloir mostly 40-45 degrees, with a ~1000 ft section at 60-65 degrees; no ice grade published.
Wikipedia: easiest route class 3 scrambling.
The Mountaineers: Strenuous 4, Technical 3; very steep gully above Charlie Brown Lake.
Normal line finishes on the summit horn's Classic Route, 5.4 (MP); approach is snow/Class 3.
Beckey (via Wikipedia): Ares Tower is a 4th class spire; trip report followed a 4th class route to the notch north of the summit, a partner soloed a low-5th west-face variation.
From Headlee Pass: Class 2 hiking and moderate snow, finishing on summit slabs with Class 3 friction scrambling depending on line.
Ridge from Kangaroo Pass mostly Class 2; scree gully before the summit has Class 3 moves (Mountaineers Technical 4 on their scramble scale).
SummitPost: Olympic guide says class 3, but other reports range class 4-5.2 for ~20 ft of poor rock above the snow; Mountaineers: short Class 4 pitch.
MP/TRs: Flight of the Falcon 5.10b/c, 7-9 pitches on Salish Peak; top of range 5.10c.
The Mountaineers: Technical 3; reports call Big and West Craggy straightforward Class 3 on loose rubbly rock, steep snow in the final gully early season.
'The class 3 east flank and the class 2 west slope' - the west slope from the Himmelhorn notch is Class 2.
Listed as 3rd class in guidebooks, but the SummitPost route page rates the rock Class 4, Grade III, and says it is not an easy class 3 scramble.
South Spur route rated 4th class; from Perfect Pass snowfields then 3rd class rock to the summit.
MP: Grade IV 5.10, 12 pitches, sustained 5.10a/b; trip report gives IV+ 5.10d.
Maintained trail from Twin Lakes to the 1935 lookout on the summit; a lingering snowfield can make it Class 2 early season.
Iron Gate trail joins the Windy Peak Trail ~2 mi south of the summit; the summit is described as a walk-up on trail.
Windy Peak Trail from Long Swamp reaches the old lookout site on the summit; a walk-up.
SummitPost: Windy Creek route difficulty 'Walk Up' - basically a walk up all the way to the summit.
MP lists one route, East Face, graded 4th (trad/alpine).
MP 'Jaw's Tooth and Northwest Ridge': 5.6, Grade II, 6 pitches; sustained 5.6 layback corner on Jaw's Tooth, then solid low 5th along the ridge to Skookum.
MP Corkscrew Route: 3rd class, 1- ice, Easy Snow; finishes with an exposed Class 3 scramble.
Popular south-side scramble described as moderate class 2 and 3 with exposure near the top.
AAJ: The Snostril (250m, WI4 M5); crux 15m of WI4 M5 exiting the cave; the Post Nasal Drip finish is also WI4 M5.
Neve Glacier then ~400 ft of 3rd/4th class scrambling; a couple of 4th-class moves at the notch below the summit.
Moderate glacier finishing with ~400 ft of 3rd/4th class rock; a couple of 4th-class moves at the notch.
MP: Free Mojo 5.11 (no letter).
MP: 5.11b, Grade III, 6 pitches; double Boving Roof on pitch 5 is the crux.
MP: Mod. Snow, 25-30 deg then 40-50 deg; 'a low 5th class move will get you to the summit'.
South Twin routes range Class 2-4 up to low 5th; the ridges are 3rd-4th class rock with occasional 5th-class moves that can be bypassed.
SummitPost: South Twin routes from Class 2-4; the west-ridge approach with the south-side gully bypass avoids the 5th-class crest and is Class 3.

SummitPost: West Ridge is the standard route, doable unroped; lots of class 3 and occasional class 4 moves with much exposure; the crest-direct finish has 5th-class moves usually bypassed by south-side gullies.
AAJ and FA TR: Spirited Away IV 5.9, ~2,000 ft, 10 pitches; crux short overhanging 5.9 on pitch 2.
WTA: semi-technical scramble with some exposure; scramble reports: most of the climb is class 3 with steep snow, a few class 4 moves reported on some lines.
North face is a narrow snow couloir, about 45+ deg at its steepest; no ice grade found (now mainly a ski descent).
SummitPost: Beckey calls the summit ridge class 3, but two short sections are decidedly class 4 and 5; a rope may be desired.
Up the bowl south of Star Lake to a pass, then the SW ridge: scree, talus and some easy scrambling with hands and feet; west side from Star Pass is Class 1-2.
Reports: a short exposed 15-ft section of class 3-4 rock near the summit, airy moves on loose rock over an exposed slab.
SummitPost: the way up Switchback is like following a trail; only scrambling is the last 300 ft over very simple large boulders.
Approach via Boiling Lake; summit from the west by easy terrain; record gives class 2-3 for the west ridge and no source rates it higher or lower.
The summit pyramid options, southeast face or west ridge, are each 'a pitch or so of low 5th class climbing'; no number given.
MP: 3rd class, 1- ice, Easy Snow; snow to 40-45 deg and short 3rd-class scrambling, some class 4 variations off route.
MP: Easy 5th, 1+ ice, Moderate Snow; Mountaineers: Grade III, 5.4, AI2, snow to 70 deg.
Alpine Grade III; slope ramps to 45-50 degrees and stays there to Liberty Cap; documented mostly as a ski descent, no ice grade given.
MP: Mod. Snow; SummitPost: Grade II, moderate glacier travel, ~30-35 degree Corridor.
MP: Mod. Snow, Grade II; ~2,200 ft of sustained 40-45 degree couloir on 30-45 degree snow/ice, usually protected with pickets.
MP lists Fuhrer Thumb as Mod. Snow; SummitPost: narrower couloir west of the Finger, Grade II on 30-45 degree snow/ice, joining the Finger at ~11,500 ft.
MP: AI1-2 Mod. Snow; Grade II with 35-50 degree snow and ice, exposed ledges protected with pickets.
MP lists Ingraham Glacier Direct as Mod. Snow; a crevassed glacier climb up the headwall with no rock and no ice grade.
MP lists WI2-3; two steps of alpine ice in the Kautz chute are the crux; the rock step is a ~25 ft rappel or downclimb off the Wapowety Cleaver, not a 5th-class climb.
No dedicated page found; the Kautz ice chute it climbs directly is WI2-3 on MP, and the record's own ice_grade puts the crux pitch at AI3.
MP: AI2-3 Steep Snow; crux is the ice of the Black Pyramid / upper ridge and the bergschrund below Liberty Cap.
MP Central Mowich Face: AI3-4 Steep Snow overall; original Grade III line takes a 40-50 degree snow ramp, the Grade IV variation has AI2-3 ice steps and 50-60 degree snow.
MP lists Tahoma Glacier as Mod. Snow: a crevassed glacier climb with no rock or ice grade.
Trip report via the Southwest Couloir: Class 2-3 scramble to the craggy summit; easiest route on the peak rated Class 3.
SummitPost: ~1,800 ft confined couloir to Nooksack Ridge, a basic snow climb with some 3rd-4th class rock at the end.
Trip report: Wall Street gully 30-35 degree snow, then the SE ridge was 'a straightforward Class 2 scramble except for 100 feet of exposed Class 3 traversing'.
SummitPost: from the Nooksack Cirque trail up the south slopes to the SE ridge, then a fractured class 3/4 ridge to the summit; reports mention two short Class 4 rock sections.
MP: 4th, AI1, Mod. Snow; Class 3-4 chimneys, steep snow at Winnie's Slide and Hell's Highway, Class 3-4 summit pyramid.

evidence: MP: AI2-3 Mod. Snow; 45-50 degree snow/ice face, summit pyramid options 4th class to 5.6.
MP: Easy 5th, AI2-3, M4, Steep Snow; the route is known as an alpine ice climb through the Price Glacier seracs.
MP: 3rd, Easy Snow; finishes with a Class 3 rock gully (snow early season) on the summit pyramid. Some sources call the pyramid Class 3-4.
MP: Easy Snow for the glacier; reaching the summit uses the summit pyramid, Class 3 on MP's Sulphide route.
From Lake of the Angels: a typical Class 2 and 3 Olympic scramble, maybe 3+ in spots, on rotten rock.
Standard summer route: a non-technical Class 2 climb over boulder ridges and ash slopes to the crater rim.
Winter route from Marble Mountain Sno-Park: a non-technical snow climb that joins Monitor Ridge below the summit; ice axe and crampons needed.
Easiest route is from First Divide (14 mi up the North Fork Skokomish), following the ridge west; rated class 1.
From Marmot Lake a creek leads into the west-side amphitheater where 'easy slopes lead to the summit'; both routes rated class 1.
Class 2/3 scramble: a gully west of the summit to the ridge, then an exposed ridge traverse; final scramble described as simple Class 2 with exposure, with Class 4/5 gendarmes avoided.
MP: 3rd, Easy Snow; St. Peter's Gate needs Class 2-3 scrambling on loose talus and scree; the west-ridge summit finish is a Class 2-3 scramble.
MP South Couloir: 4th; 'mostly 2nd and 3rd class with ... one step of 4th class terrain near the summit pinnacle' (Olympic guide says 3rd class).
MP South Couloir: 4th; mostly 2nd-3rd class with one 4th-class step on the east side of the summit pinnacle.
MP lists King Kong - Gorillas Direct Direct at 5.12a; crux is the two-pitch direct headwall finish.
MP: AI2-3 Steep Snow, Grade III, 2,000 ft (Prater, Prater, Mahre 1957).
MP: WI2-3 M5-; mostly 40-50 degree snow with a narrow 60-80 degree ice step as the crux, then a low-to-mid 5th West Ridge finish.
MP: 4th, Mod. Snow; other descriptions give Grade II, snow to 40 degrees, then simple Class 3 ridge scrambling to the summit.
SummitPost: the Southwest Ridge route is Class 2, with optional Class 3 bypasses; trip reports note a few Class 2-3 rock steps on a steep boot track.
Long trail via Rachor Pass; 'a short hike and an easy rock scramble' to the rounded summit.
MP lists East Ridge/SE Face at 5.8; the Cascade Alpine Guide gives a 4-pitch 5.6, but trip reports call the first pitch a hard 5.8 (40 ft vertical, offwidth or finger crack).
Maintained Mt. Townsend Trail #839 to the summit: 8.2 mi round trip, 2,900 ft gain, no scrambling.
MP: 5.6 PG13; other sources give 5.7 for the short offwidth crux, with mostly 4th and low-5th ridge climbing.
Easiest route: scramble class 3 via the West Side or Gray Wolf Ridge.
Standard south route: Grade I, Class 3, with the 'hourglass' a short pitch of 4th class climbing on the way to the summit.
MP: Winter Direct 4th, AI1-2 Steep Snow, Grade II; climbed only when snow-covered, with two tools and rock and ice protection.
Anderson's Thumb (~6,850 ft subpeak of Mount Anderson) is described only as 'a fun rock climb on good sandstone'; no numeric grade found online. Record says Class 4 / low 5th.
Beckey calls the SW ridge 3rd class, but glacial recession now leaves a low-5th pitch at its base; summit tower low 5th (chockstone 5.2).
Record's own difficulty at the top of its range; low-confidence research (Class 2) not adopted.
The Amphitheater (Cape Disappointment) on Mountain Project lists 4 climbs and describes gullies used as 3rd-class access/descent; the individual route grade was not visible.

South-side rib and gully from Entiat Meadows to the east ridge at 7,900 ft, a non-technical scramble on scree and heather; no class rating stated
West ridge is mostly hiking, then 'fun scrambling' to the true summit (no class given); the record's 4th class finish could not be confirmed or refuted.
AAJ FA account: 300 ft of rock, then a 300-ft 50-degree ice patch, then easier upslab rock; no modern grade found.
Easiest route listed as Class 4 (West Face); FA account quoted by the record (easy-moderate fifth class) not found online.
Beckey: mainly class 4 with one lead of moderate class 5; no number published.
Trip report via the South Gully and East Ridge: a snow defile with moats, then a Class 2-3 scramble to the top; no 5th-class climbing mentioned. The record's own breakdown tops out at Class 3-4.
South/SE face from Klawatti Col: 45-50° snow through a constriction (icy at times, bergschrund bridges) in early season; later it melts out to slabs with a moat.
Trip reports: X Couloir is 60+ degree exposed snow/ice with a narrow crux gully near 75 degrees, climbed with tools and screws; no published ice grade.
MP: West Face 'Easy 5th', with no number anywhere.
Luahna's summit scramble is reported as Class 2-3 (Pilz/Walrus side); one TR found a direct south-side line about 4th class.
MP: East Ridge 'Easy 5th'; no numbered grade found.
MP: Easy 5th, Grade II; mostly Class 3 with a 'Class 4/5' slabby-depression crux.
Peakbagger only notes an ascent via the Massie Lake High Route and summit ridge (3 logged ascents); no class rating found online, so the record's top-of-range Class 3 is kept.
MP: South Face (Crooks/Kennedy 1941) Easy 5th, Grade II, 4 pitches; several low-5th pitches, a steeper final pitch, no numbers.
Described as Grade IV, ~55 degree snow/ice in 4-5 pitches up chimneys of the Roosevelt Cliff; extremely dangerous from rock- and icefall. No source gives an ice grade.
SummitPost: Grade III, 45-50 degree snow/ice wall over several pitches and a narrow snow arete; AAJ 1971 line: 60 degree snow/ice face. No source gives an AI grade.
No online description of a North Ridge route on Chaval was found; the record's own grade (5.6-5.7, two technical pitches) is read at the top of its range.
Sources list the easiest route only as 'scrambling' (a Mountaineers Olympia scramble peak); no class number found, so the top of the record's range is kept.
Degenhardt South Route described as low 5th (another report calls it a '4th class summit'); one party off route roped up for ~5.7. No number given for the normal line.
Mountaineers: Class 4 ramps across the E face, then up to the summit with a Class 5 step; no number given.
First climbed 1948 (Molenaar, Craig); route listings give Alpine Grade III with ice to ~60 degrees; no published AI grade.
MP grades the wall M5+ X, Grade V (a mixed grade); other sources say it is not technically hard by modern standards and the danger is the 300 ft serac band.
Mountain Project: Luna Glacier 'Easy 5th', Steep Snow, M1c; no numeric rock grade found anywhere.
Record's own difficulty at the top of its range; low-confidence research (Class 4) not adopted.

1952 FA account: ~500 ft of difficult rock to the Pernod-Chianti notch, two hard leads with pitons, a pendulum and a sling near the summit; no modern free grade found online beyond the record's 5.5-5.7.
MP: Open Book rated 'Easy 5th' (no number), left-leaning cracks east of The Roof.
Trip report: from Degenhardt, 3rd-4th class with a few moves of low 5th to leave the ridge onto Pyramid; no number anywhere.
Little route-specific beta; Middle Finger described as the hardest-looking of the three, with class 4 scrambling reported.
Record's own difficulty at the top of its range; low-confidence research (5.4) not adopted.
South-side routes from Perfect Pass/Whatcom Glacier: snowfields then 3rd class rock to the summit; no separate grade found for a 'Southwest Route'.
Same NW Shoulder line; steep snow/ice to ~50-55 degrees and Class 3-4 summit rock (later season); no published ice grade found.
